cards.explanation: The answer is a fig tree, friends, just like Mark says. Jesus spots it in the distance, covered in leaves, and walks over to look for fruit. I think a tree in leaf looks promising from far off. It's like a cookie box that looks full from across the room and turns out to hold nothing but crumbs.
The answer is False, friends. Jesus reaches the tree and finds nothing on it except leaves. No sneaky figs tucked behind a branch. Mark tells us it was not the season for figs.

The answer is that Jesus says, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” Notice He's talking right to the tree, friends. That's a strange thing to see, and I think the disciples were watching closely.
The answer is True, friends. Mark says it plainly: “And His disciples heard this statement.” So they heard what Jesus said to the tree. That matters when we get to the next morning.

The answer is that He begins to drive them out, friends. Jesus enters the temple courts and begins to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves. I think that got everybody's attention.
The answer is money changers, friends. Mark says Jesus “…overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.” I think that courtyard got loud in a hurry.
The answer is merchandise, friends. Mark says Jesus would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts. Notice that it's anyone, not just the sellers. He wouldn't allow it.

The answer is a house of prayer for all the nations, friends. Jesus asks, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’?” That's what He points them back to. Prayer, and room for all the nations.

The answer is a den of robbers, friends. After the house of prayer line, Jesus tells them, “But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’…” It's a sharp contrast with what the house was meant to be. Prayer on one side, a den of robbers on the other.

The answer is kill, friends, and it's a heavy one. Mark says the chief priests and scribes looked for a way to kill Him. I think this is a part where we slow down and let it sit. The story is getting serious.
The answer is False, friends. Mark says they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching. So the crowd is amazed, not turning away. The fear comes from that.

The answer is withered, friends, and all the way down. Mark says they saw the fig tree withered from its roots. Peter remembers it and calls it the tree Jesus cursed. That's quite a change from the leaves Jesus saw on it earlier.

The answer is Peter, friends, one of Jesus' disciples. Mark says Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.” He's the one who connects the tree to what Jesus said the day before. Good memory on that man.

The answer is that Jesus tells them to have faith in God, friends. He says, “Have faith in God…” Peter points at a tree, and Jesus points them to God. Everything else in this part grows out of that line.
The answer is False, friends. Jesus says it will be done for the one who “…has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen…” So doubt isn't in the picture. Belief is what He describes.

The answer is to believe that you have received it, friends. Jesus tells them, “…whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.” He moves the mountain picture straight into prayer. Believe, and it will be yours.

The answer is to forgive what you hold against them, friends. Jesus says, “…if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.” He says it for the moment you stand to pray. It's a simple instruction, and it's not an easy one.

The answer is True, friends. Jesus says to forgive, “…so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.” He ties the two together in the same sentence. It's a lot to take in, and it's worth reading slowly.
